stories.title: FBI's criminal information database hacked, CNN reports
summary: The FBI is investigating a suspected breach of a nationwide database ​used by federal, state and local ‌law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information, CNN reported on Friday, citing two people briefed ​on the investigation.

The apparent compromise of the ​National Crime Information Centre database would ⁠mark the second intrusion involving an FBI ​system in recent months and the latest in ​a string of cyber incidents that have alarmed US officials over the past week.

Read: FBI and US Secret Service working with Binance after $6.3 billion hack, source says The FBI database is used by law enforcement ‌agencies ⁠nationwide to store and share information on warrants, criminal histories and background checks.

stories.title: Parliamentary affairs minister invites PTI to join NA electoral reforms committee
summary: The government on Saturday invited the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to join the National Assembly (NA) Electoral Reforms Committee (ERC), offering representation in proportion to the party’s strength in the lower house while rejecting its demand for equal representation.
The NA on October 16 passed a motion moved by Dr Chaudhry under Rule 244B to form a parliamentary committee comprising members from both houses to recommend electoral reforms.
The motion stipulated that parliamentary parties would be represented in proportion to their strength in Parliament.

stories.title: EU proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
summary: The EU put forward plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to fund its next budget Saturday, as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc's long-term funding.

European Council President Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros ($224 billion) a plan initially put forward by the European Commission, which some countries had slammed as too onerous.

Among these could be a tax on digital firms, which the draft Costa presented Saturday says will concern companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU as well as a global turnover of more than 750 million euros.

stories.title: From screens in class to smart glasses, Norway rethinks new technologies
summary: After making laptops and screens ubiquitous in schools across the country, Norway is bringing back textbooks in a bid to reverse a sharp decline in pupils' reading and writing skills.

"There is reason to believe that the introduction of screens in schools happened too quickly, before we had sufficient knowledge about their effects and about what constitutes good pedagogical use of digital devices," Norway's Digitalisation Minister Torgeir Micaelsen told AFP.
'Quick fixes' Norwegian authorities have, in turn, recommended regulating the use of mobile phones in schools and introducing artificial intelligence into the school curriculum only gradually.

stories.title: Anthropic claims AI-assisted breakthrough on 167-year-old math problem
summary: A mathematician at the US artificial intelligence company Anthropic on Friday claimed that he and the company's Claude AI model have solved the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis, one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems.
Levent Alpoge said he discovered a proof of the hypothesis, first proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859.
"I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," Alpoge wrote in a four-page statement published on his website.

stories.title: Videos, photos of 13-year-old domestic worker's torture at senior FIA official’s Islamabad residence emerge
summary: Read: Court extends remand of two suspects in Fatima murder case Earlier, a post-mortem report prepared by the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) revealed extensive injuries and signs of prolonged and brutal torture inflicted on the child.

Read: Court extends remand of two suspects in Fatima murder case Fatima was working as a domestic helper at the residence, which police identified as the official accommodation of a senior FIA officer located within the Islamabad Police Lines Headquarters.
The death of 13-year-old Fatima Asghar has once again drawn attention to the exploitation and abuse of children employed as domestic workers in Pakistan.

stories.title: Bangladesh border guards detain six Indians attempting illegal border crossing
summary: Nalitabari Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Kamal Hossain said the BGB had handed over the six individuals, including three children, to the police station on Friday night after they had been detained earlier in the Fekamari area in the upazila, according to the TOB.

According to the BGB, during preliminary questioning, the detainees stated that they had illegally entered Bangladesh through the border in 2024 and had been staying in different parts of the country ever since.
Bayezid added that the BGB would continue its strict stance against drug trafficking, smuggling and illegal border crossings, the TOB reported.

stories.title: NIH issues nationwide advisories on flu, smog and vaccine-preventable diseases
summary: The advisories, issued by the NIH’s Centre for Disease Control, cover the prevention and control of seasonal influenza for 2026-27, health risks and precautionary measures associated with smog, as well as vaccine-preventable disease control.
Health authorities have further been directed to strengthen public awareness and risk communication to promote preventive measures against seasonal infections and smog-related health complications.
The NIH has urged all relevant health authorities and stakeholders across the country to implement the recommended measures promptly to minimise winter-related health risks and protect public health.

stories.title: Nearly 1,500 people stranded in Japan's Fukushima Prefecture due to heavy snow
summary: Nearly 1,500 people were stranded in a village in Japan's Fukushima Prefecture after heavy snow toppled trees and blocked roads, local authorities said on Saturday.

Those stranded include approximately 900 residents and 500 people staying at hotels and other accommodations in and around the Urabandai area of Kitashiobara village, Kyodo News Agency reported, citing authorities.
No injuries have been reported so far, according to authorities.

stories.title: How Grand Theft Auto VI's launch surpassed expectations
summary: I'm just kind of soaking in the world." Read: GTA 6 reportedly beats Taylor Swift’s $2 billion Eras Tour record in just one day Even rival developers were complimentary.
Rockstar said on Friday that retail sales of the game reached a record $3.79 billion, their estimate as of the end of launch day.
It kind of just shows the growth of video games as a medium as well, artistically, commercially and culturally.” The action in GTA VI is set in Leonida, the game's take on Florida.

stories.title: As Trump basks in summit pomp, China's Xi strengthens his hand
summary: US President Donald Trump hailed the fanfare of his meeting this week with Xi Jinping as a victory, but the US president has gained little from three such summits this year while the Chinese ​leader has strengthened his position on the world stage, analysts say.

Xi emerged from a global gathering in China as a statesman who could convene the first China-US-Russia summit and he keeps a ‌fragile trade truce with the US in a holding pattern — where Beijing likes it — even as Washington takes a harder line.

"It may ​feel like a holding pattern by comparison to past summits, but in the current context it's actually a significant step, given the recent midterm elections and the Jensen Huang scandal." Analysts expect the year's fourth Trump-Xi meeting will also be heavy on optics.

stories.title: Hafiz Naeem urges government to prioritise public relief in meeting with Naqvi
summary: Later on October 27, Shehbaz also met Hafiz Naeem in Islamabad and agreed to form a six-member committee to finalise recommendations on expanding the existing petrol relief scheme and preparing proposals for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy.

Read: JI to continue protests nationwide as it demands end to petroleum levy He stated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Hafiz Naeem were expected to meet on November 24 or 25 to finalise a mechanism for reducing the petroleum levy and providing relief to consumers.
In regards to JI's negotiation with the government, Hafiz Naeem stated that the party had presented the final draft of its demands regarding the petroleum levy and other taxes to the government.

stories.title: Musadik Malik warns of climate threat to civilisation, heritage at SCO forum in New Delhi
summary: Malik described Pakistan’s cultural identity as a product of diverse civilisations, communities and historical influences, saying the country’s heritage has been shaped by centuries of interaction among people from different regions.

Malik also held a bilateral meeting with Tajikistan’s Minister of Culture, Sattoriyon Amonzoda, on the sidelines of the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, the Pakistan High Commission in India said in a post on X.

Earlier, Dr Musadik Malik also stressed the importance of civilisational dialogue among regional countries, including Pakistan and India, saying that cultures and historical connections transcend geographical and political boundaries.

stories.title: DPM Dar calls for new regional security framework to ensure lasting peace
summary: Highlighting China's involvement in the peace efforts, Dar said Pakistan and China had proposed a five-point peace initiative that received substantial backing from major international actors, including the European Union and the United Kingdom.
Dar attributed Pakistan's economic instability to policy shortcomings but expressed confidence in the country's resilience and its potential to join the G20 in the future.

Speaking about Pakistan's relations with the European Union, Dar pledged a comprehensive security mechanism to protect investors in the country, citing measures including the imposition of emergency and governor's rule to safeguard economic interests.

stories.title: US Vice President Vance declines to say he would have ordered Iran strikes
summary: Many viewed his statement, posted on social media, as a break with Trump as the vice president considers a 2028 White House bid.

"But I say, I know the Iranians, and, frankly, they're crazy." When asked later in the press conference if the war was worth Republicans' steep congressional losses, Vance did not explicitly endorse the operation.

And my view is that my goal is and my job is to support the president of the United States." Vance has long opposed the war and acted as Washington's main emissary for peace talks, brokering a short-lived provisional truce over the summer that quickly fell apart.

stories.title: Fazl calls for transparent elections, criticises government over provincial rights
summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Saturday called for transparent elections, saying they were necessary to address the country’s problems, while criticising the government over its handling of provincial rights, security and political affairs.
Fazl said his party was not against the military, describing it as the country’s defence force.
Fazl said his party welcomed investment in the country but alleged that those who opposed a particular narrative were threatened with the opening of cases against them.

stories.title: Australia gives Cummins unanimous backing as captain
summary: Cricket Australia (CA) backed Pat Cummins to remain as captain of the test and one-day international sides on Saturday and rejected any suggestion his integrity had ​been compromised amid the renewed furore over the 2018 ball-tampering incident.
"We've expressed our support to Pat and our ​concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," ​Cricket Australia Chairman David Boon said in a statement.
Cummins welcomed the board's support and confirmed ​he would ⁠participate in the process.

stories.title: Pakistan, Indonesia conclude third edition of bilateral counter-terrorism exercise Elang Strike-III
summary: The Pakistan Army and Indonesian Army concluded the third edition of the bilateral counter-terrorism exercise, Elang Strike-III, at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) in Pabbi, the military’s media wing said on Saturday.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), "the exercise focused on sharing counter-terrorism experiences, refining operational drills and procedures, and enhancing combat skills through mutual learning and the exchange of best practices".

On May 7, Pakistan and Sri Lanka concluded a two-week-long joint counter-terrorism exercise at Tarbela, focused on enhancing counter-terrorism skills and strengthening their longstanding military-to-military relations.

stories.title: Mohammad Rizwan, Shan Masood, Saim Ayub dropped as PCB unveils central contracts
summary: Pakistan’s Test captain Babar Azam and Salman Ali Agha are the only two players awarded contracts covering both Test and one-day international cricket.

Azan Awais, Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Abbas and Sajid Khan have been included in the Test category while Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Faheem Ashraf, Haris Rauf and Shaheen Shah Afridi have received ODI and T20I contracts.
Pakistan's T20I captain Sahibzada Farhan, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Salman Mirza, Naseem Shah, Shadab Khan and Usman Tariq make up the T20I-only category.

stories.title: Meta's India offices hit by opposition protests over account removals
summary: The youth wing of India's main opposition ​Congress party clashed with police outside Meta offices, protesting the company's removal of some Instagram accounts of its members, ‌according to footage released by the group on Saturday.
Debate is growing in India about potential risks to free speech from the increasingly strict efforts of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government ​to remove social media content it objects to.
Congress has long accused Meta and other social ⁠media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi's government.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says it intercepts three Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh
summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Saturday it had intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh, marking the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in a few days, after its tallest skyscraper was struck on Thursday.

The latest attack followed an escalation in cross-border strikes on Friday, when the Saudi-led coalition said it had struck the Red Sea port of Hodeidah and carried out operations targeting Houthi missile and drone capabilities in the capital, Sanaa.

Separately, the army noted strikes on Friday by the Saudi-led coalition against facilities at the Hudaydah port in western Yemen and sites in the capital Sanaa that it said were being used by the Houthis to support military operations.

stories.title: India on top in first New Zealand Test
summary: KL Rahul made 136 and Shubman Gill 98 as India were 486-4 at the close of play Saturday in the first Test against New Zealand, a lead of 118 runs with two days remaining.
Kyle Jamieson was the best of New Zealand's bowlers taking 1-57, while Duffy ended the day with the fourth most expensive figures in New Zealand's Test history, with 1-180 from 29 overs.
India had resumed at 159-1 to start the day, a deficit of 209 runs, with Rahul on 52 and Padikkal on 16.

stories.title: New caravan of about 300 migrants crosses into southern Mexico
summary: A caravan of about 300 migrants, mostly from Central America, crossed into southern Mexico on Friday to join a larger group heading north, a week after United States President Donald Trump threatened fresh tariffs on Mexico if it did not halt the movement.

Read: Trump's personalised diplomacy hits its limits with 3-way summit "We’ve thought about staying in Mexico to work, until Donald Trump leaves office," said Herson David Escalante, a Honduran national, as he walked as part of the new caravan.
Last week, Trump threatened to double tariffs on goods from Mexico if its authorities did not stop the caravan.

stories.title: Iraq fire at Basra power station kills at least four, injures 30
summary: At least 4 people were killed and 30 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.
Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.
The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday strongly condemned the Houthi attack on the King Abdullah Financial District in Riyadh, describing it as an act of “reckless aggression” targeting civilian infrastructure and economic facilities.

The latest attack followed an escalation in cross-border strikes on Friday, when the Saudi-led coalition said it had struck the Red Sea port of Hodeidah and carried out operations targeting Houthi missile and drone capabilities in the capital, Sanaa.

On October 26, Pakistan strongly condemned "reprehensible" Houthi ballistic missile attacks on October 24, which had targeted the Makkah and Madinah regions of Saudi Arabia, including areas in the vicinity of the holy sites.

stories.title: Trump vows to make ‘permanent’ deal with Iran, prevent future nuclear ambitions
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he intended to secure a “permanent” deal with Iran, insisting that no future American president should be able to allow Tehran to obtain a nuclear weapon.

Follow: https://t.co/GHI09iA8ru pic.twitter.com/fnVToCKWlP — Press TV 🔻 (@PressTV) November 21, 2026 Iran also released a video showcasing a new underground "missile city", featuring a double-missile launcher.

Trump, in a press conference on Friday, said: "They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me." The United States and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to retaliate against Israel and Gulf states hosting US military bases.

stories.title: NAB challenges plea against FCC jurisdiction
summary: The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) has questioned the maintainability of a petition challenging amendments to the accountability law that transferred jurisdiction over second appeals in NAB cases from the Supreme Court to the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC).

The Islamabad High Court (IHC), while hearing the plea on Friday, sought arguments from NAB on the maintainability of the petition at the next hearing and adjourned the proceedings without fixing a date for further hearing.
The petition challenges an amendment under which appellate jurisdiction in NAB cases, following decisions by high courts, was shifted from the Supreme Court to the FCC.

stories.title: Mustafa Kamal links MQM-P's demand for new provinces to failure of local governments
summary: Kamal's remarks came amid an escalating political row between the MQM-P and the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) over the creation of new provinces.
The proposal drew the interest of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P), which has repeatedly advocated carving out new provinces from Sindh.
Speaking about another major public health challenge, Kamal said approximately 11 million people had been identified with Hepatitis C during screening in Pakistan.

stories.title: PTI backs referendum to determine public opinion on creation of new provinces
summary: Dogar said PTI founder Imran Khan had consistently advocated the creation of smaller provinces, adding that a separate South Punjab province had been included in the party's 2018 election manifesto.

Read: Govt moves to break deadlock over new provinces through political dialogue Dogar said divisions within the ruling coalition made it premature for the opposition to decide its position on the proposed constitutional amendment.
On the proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, Dogar said government Chief Whip Tariq Fazal Chaudhry had asked the opposition to nominate its members.
